question: REPowerEU is funding the energy and structural retrofitting of four publicly-owned apartment blocks (Nos 30 and 30a in Via Lulli and Nos 43 and 47 in Via Porpora) in Milan, a project put forward by the Lombardy Regional Executive and ALER, the city’s housing agency.

The tenants’ association and certain trade unions have, however, pointed out that the plan entails the compulsory rehousing of the residents concerned – including a great many elderly people, persons living with disabilities, vulnerable families and households with children – for a period of up to three years in accommodation that could be located in another district.

It also appears that ALER has already entertained the notion of resorting to forced evictions. The residents and trade unions concerned have proposed staggering the retrofitting works and using the 100 or so flats at No 47, Via Porpora, to temporarily house tenants so that they can remain in the neighbourhood and avoid disruptions to their social networks and care and welfare arrangements.
In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission hold that the ALER-Lombardy Region project’s arrangements uphold the rights enshrined in the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights?

Will it verify whether the Lulli-Porpora project and its implementation comply with the conditions – particularly those concerning the protection of vulnerable residents – laid down for the use of REPowerEU funds?

Will the Commission call on the competent authorities to assess the alternative plan proposed by the Lulli-Porpora tenants and ensure that the latter are genuinely involved in the project going forwards?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.11.2026) The Commission notes that the Honourable Members’ question seems to relate to Investment 17 ‘Financial instrument for energy renovations of public residential housing’ under Mission 7 of the Italian Recovery and Resilience Plan1.

The measure consists of a public investment in a facility, namely the ‘Financial instrument to alleviate energy poverty’, aimed to incentivise private investment in combination with public support. The facility targets energy renovations projects in public residential housing achieving on average at least a 30% of primary energy demand reduction.

The Commission notes that this measure envisages a final target (M7-49)2 under the tenth payment request, which has recently been submitted by Italy and is currently under assessment by the Commission. As this assessment is ongoing, the Commission is not in a position to further comment at this stage.
The assessment concerns the fulfilment of that target and not the implementation of individual projects, which remains the responsibility of the Member State.

Nevertheless, the Commission recalls that, without prejudice to its role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible for the compliance of projects financed by their recovery and resilience plans with EU and national law, including the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights when they are implementing Union law.

In this context, under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) Regulation3, Member States are required to include a summary of the consultation process, conducted in accordance with the national legal framework and to complement it where a REPowerEU chapter has been included.
1 ST 12357/26 ADD 1, ANNEX to the COUNCIL IMPLEMENTING DECISION amending the Implementing

Decision of 13 July 2021 on the approval of the assessment of the recovery and resilience plan for Italy. 2 The concerned target requires, inter alia, the implementing partner of the Facility to enter into legal agreements with final beneficiaries for an amount necessary to use 100% of the RRF investment into the Facility.

3 Article 18(4)(q), Regulation (EU) 2021/241 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 February 2021 establishing the Recovery and Resilience Facility, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/241/2023-0301/eng.
